title: Plate Tectonics
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Plate Tectonics Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: The theory of plate tectonics is the unifying theory that explains Earth's geological processes: Earth's layers, plate boundaries, earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain building, and BC's location on the Ring of Fire. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 8, Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets (BC): Earth's layers, evidence for plate tectonics, plate boundaries, earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Earth's crust is broken into moving plates.
key_sub: Plates move a few centimetres a year.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth has a crust, mantle, outer core and inner core. The crust and upper mantle are broken into plates that float on the hotter mantle below. Convection currents in the mantle move the plates a few centimetres each year.

At plate boundaries plates move apart (divergent), collide (convergent) or slide past each other (transform). This makes earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains. Off the BC coast, the Juan de Fuca plate slides under the North American plate, so BC has earthquakes and volcanoes such as Mount Garibaldi.

Example

Which layer of Earth do we live on?

The thinnest, outer layer

Answer: the crust

Example

What happens at a convergent boundary?

Plates move toward each other.

Answer: plates collide

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the plates float on liquid magma all the way through.
  • Thinking plates move fast enough to see.
  • Mixing up the crust and the core.

items.q: Who first proposed continental drift using fossils and continent shapes?
items.e: He proposed it in 1912.

items.q: About how fast do plates move?

items.q: Benjamin studies the Himalayas, where plates push together. What kind of plate boundary is it?

items.q: What often happens where an ocean plate meets a continental plate?

items.q: Liam studies Iceland splitting slowly, where plates move apart. What kind of plate boundary is it?

items.q: Do continents float on the ocean?
c: No. Continents are part of plates that move over the hot, slowly flowing mantle.
items.e: The mantle rock can flow very slowly.

items.q: Olivia studies the Alpine Fault in New Zealand. What happens to the plates there?

items.e: The Alpine Fault in New Zealand is at a transform boundary.

items.q: What are tectonic plates?
c: large pieces of Earth's outer layer (lithosphere) that slowly move
items.e: Continents and ocean floors ride on plates.
